questions.subject: Civil Engineering
questions.questionMarkup:
Consider the following statements in reference to transformation of stresses:
1. In case of two like and equal principal stresses, the resultant stress on any plane is equal to the principal stresses.
2. In case of two equal and unlike stresses, the resultant stress on any plane is equal to principal stresses.
3. In case of two like and equal principal stresses, the obliquity of the resultant stress is on any plane is zero.
4. In a strained material subjected to two dimensional stresses, the sum of normal stresses on any two mutually perpendicular planes is equal to the sum of major and minor principal stresses.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.questionText: Consider the following statements in reference to transformation of stresses: 1. In case of two like and equal principal stresses, the resultant stress on any plane is equal to the principal stresses. 2. In case of two like and equal principal stresses, the obliquity of the resultant stress is on any plane is zero. 4. In a strained material subjected to two dimensional stresses, the sum of normal stresses on any two mutually perpendicular planes is equal to the sum of major and minor principal stresses. Which of the above statements are correct?

questions.questionText: Consider the following statements: 1. Shear stresses on two mutually normal planes are equal in magnitude and direction. 2. The sum of normal stresses on mutually normal planes is equal to the sum of principal stresses. Of the above statements, which is / are true ?
questions.explanationHtml:
(c)
Shear stresses on two mutually normal i.e. perpendicular planes are equal in magnitude but opposite in direction.
